summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, peripheral vascular disease, and prior pacemaker infection was admitted for worsening pain and erythema in the right foot due to a non-healing plantar ulcer. He presented to his podiatrist with three days of increasing symptoms and was found to have cellulitis. Initial X-ray showed no osteomyelitis but a possible foreign body near the ulcer. He was started on IV vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam for infection. Vascular studies revealed severe bilateral aortoiliac and tibial disease, and vascular surgery recommended a toe amputation. The patient requested a second opinion and elected to transfer to another hospital under the care of his cardiologist. During the stay, he remained afebrile, with stable cardiac status and good glycemic control. His AV fistula was evaluated for steal syndrome with digital ischemia in the left hand, but he declined surgical intervention due to prior infection risks. He was discharged in stable condition for transfer to extended care at another facility.
